svg.title: A conull carrier with null topological support
svg.desc: Exact implication diagram for Lemma 3.13, Proposition 3.14 and Corollary 3.15. A locally countable conull Borel carrier in a closed set has no positive compact subset, while its nonempty closed support is null. Adding dense atoms creates full support and an invariant set of intermediate mass.

g.text: A compact carrier can have null support
Schematic implications · the original topology and Borel subsets are retained
Hypotheses of Proposition 3.14
X compact Hausdorff · μ(X) = 1 · all singleton masses are zero
D closed · Y ⊆ D Borel · μ(Y) = 1
Every y ∈ Y has an ambient open Uᵧ with Uᵧ ∩ D countable.
Null neighborhoods
μ(Uᵧ) = 0 for every y ∈ Y; X ∖ D is also open and null.
Every compact C ⊆ Y has a finite such cover: C is countable and μ(C) = 0.
The support Sμ is nonempty and closed, but has mass zero.
∅ ≠ Sμ ⊆ D ∖ Y · μ(Sμ) = 0 · μ(X ∖ Sμ) = 1
X ∖ Sμ is an arbitrary union of null open sets; every countable subunion is null.
Lemma 3.13: nonsingular homeomorphisms preserve Sμ exactly.
Equivalent measure / support restriction
Same support Sμ; its mass is still zero.
Restricting μ to Sμ gives zero measure.
Corollary 3.15 · no full-support repair
Add dense positive point masses
Full support; the point atoms Q have λ(Q) = t.
Every nonsingular bijection preserves Q.
Corollary 3.15 · ergodicity fails
Source comparison and remaining decision
Wage's compared diagonal properties fit the null-support test.
The full standard-measure, free, ergodic, full-support atomless question remains open.
